question.text: A person invites a party of 10 friends at dinner and place them so that 4 are on one round table and 6 on the other round table. The number of ways in which he can arrange the guests is

solution.text:
Selection of 6 guests $=10 \mathrm{C} 6$ 

Permutation of 6 on round table $=5 !$ 

Permutation of 4 on round table $=3 !$

Then, total number of arrangements $=10 \mathrm{C} 6.5 ! .3 !$

$=\frac{(10) !}{6 ! 4 !} \cdot 5 ! .3 !=\frac{(10) !}{24}$
